subject: Regional Binding Letter and VPC Egress Controls - BlueHarbor
messages:
From: Amelia Song <amelia.song@blueharbor.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: security@blueharbor.com, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Binding wording + VPC egress controls for procurement

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement needs two items to move BlueHarbor onto Redwood for inference: a short regional binding letter (US-only residency commitment for production payloads) and a technical note describing VPC/private-link egress controls (how customer traffic is kept within their VPC and any egress-to-internet controls).

Can you provide a draft of the wording your legal/compliance team would sign, and a diagram plus short bullets for our security team that explain egress behavior and where logs/audit records live?

Timeline: procurement wants these by COB Thursday (22 Jul) to include in the purchase order.

Appreciate it — if you need to loop in infra folks please do.

—Amelia
Head of Procurement, BlueHarbor Pharma
(Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Song <amelia.song@blueharbor.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Binding wording + VPC egress controls for procurement

Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Attaching a draft Regional Binding Letter and a VPC egress architecture diagram for your security and procurement teams to review. Quick summary below before Monica adds technical detail: 

- Regional commitment: Redwood confirms production inference payloads for your account can be restricted to the US region and routed only over private connectivity options (Redwood Dedicated / Private deployment with VPC endpoints). Draft language attached.
- Private-link / VPC egress: We support Private Link (VPC endpoint) + optional NAT restrictions. Default behavior for a Private deployment: no public internet egress from customer compute; optional outbound egress policies (allow-list) for managed telemetry endpoints.
- Audit & retention: Audit logs for inference requests and infrastructure events are retained per the agreed retention in the PO (we included a SOC 2 snapshot).

Action items:
1) Security: please review the attached diagram and technical bullets and tell us if you need additional KMS partitioning language.
2) Procurement: if the draft binding letter looks fine we can push to DocuSign and attach the signed copy to the PO.

Attaching: redwood_regional_binding_letter_draft.pdf, vpc-egress-architecture-2026-07.png, SOC2-snapshot-2026-07.pdf

Thanks — I’ll stand by for comments.

—Priyom Das
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
(Attachment: redwood_regional_binding_letter_draft.pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Binding wording + VPC egress controls for procurement

Amelia — adding a short technical note from infra: 

Summary (technical):
- Deployment model: BlueHarbor will use Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed networking). The inference workers run in a private subnet inside your VPC.
- Egress behavior: By default there is no internet egress from the inference subnet. Outbound network flows are controlled by customer route tables and security groups. If you enable "managed telemetry" we can route telemetry to an allow-listed telemetry endpoint over Private Link; otherwise telemetry can be disabled.
- KMS / keys: Customer keys are supported via KMS integration. Keys are scoped per-customer; we do not share customer keys across accounts. We can add stronger language around key partitioning if required by procurement.
- Audit & evidence: Request/response logs and audit traces are written to a customer-managed S3 (or encrypted storage) bucket in the chosen region. We can provide time-limited read artifacts or an exports pack for your audit team.

If it helps, we can produce a 1-page runbook describing emergency fallback steps and how we handle cross-region failovers (we will not failover out-of-region without an explicit config change).

Let me know what additional technical detail you need for security sign-off.

—Monica Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: vpc-egress-architecture-2026-07.png)
